key_insight: The paper identifies a failure mode called sink-collapse—where autoregressive long-form video models repeatedly revert to an attention "sink" frame—and introduces targeted architectural and training fixes that restore long-term temporal coherence, enabling generation that scales toward hour-long videos.
problem_solved: Mitigates error accumulation and cyclic scene resets in autoregressive long-form video generation by diagnosing and preventing sink-frame driven collapse, improving continuity and realistic long-term dynamics.
method: Diagnose and quantify sink-collapse to reveal how sink-frame attention causes abrupt resets and cyclic motion patterns.
Introduce a sink-aware attention design plus anti-collapse regularization to discourage repeated reversion to the sink frame during generation.
Use hierarchical temporal context (chunked decoding with a persistent latent memory) to preserve long-range dynamics and scale autoregressive decoding to hour-long outputs.
impact: Makes autoregressive video generators more reliable for long-form outputs, reducing repetitive artifacts and improving coherence across minutes-to-hours—useful for simulation, film/VFX, and long-form content generation research and products.
visual_elements: Before/after timeline showing sink-collapse (repeating sink frame, abrupt resets) vs stabilized long-term generation
Model architecture diagram highlighting sink-aware attention and hierarchical/persistent memory pathways
Line chart comparing coherence metrics (e.g., temporal consistency, diversity) vs generated duration for baseline and proposed method
Example frame sequences or GIF strips demonstrating eliminated cyclic motion and sustained scene dynamics
paper_title: LoL: Longer than Longer, Scaling Video Generation to Hour
paper_authors: Justin Cui, Jie Wu, Ming Li, Tao Yang, Xiaojie Li
